priorTitle: Principal of the normal department
priorInstitution: Arkansas Industrial University (same institution, internal appointment)
notes: Second, non-acting term leading the university, returning to the presidency from the normal department after Albert Bishop's departure. He later became superintendent of the Fort Smith school district (1884) and of Fayetteville public schools (1889).

priorTitle: Superintendent
notes: West Point graduate (1842) and Confederate lieutenant general who had chaired mathematics at Washington College and Davidson College before running the North Carolina Military Institute. His administration raised academic standards and grew enrollment; he resigned in 1884 for health reasons.

priorTitle: Professor of Mathematics
notes: Virginia-born former Confederate officer whose administration emphasized institutional regulation, holding forty-two faculty meetings before Christmas of his first college year. He resigned in 1887 in opposition to a General Assembly reorganization of the university.

priorTitle: Chair of Mathematics and Logic (then acting president)
priorInstitution: Arkansas Industrial University (same institution, internal appointment)
notes: Promoted from the mathematics and logic chair (1885-1887) to acting president and then confirmed as the university's fifth president. Student attendance rose to roughly 700 during his tenure, which a faculty report called a period of progress unprecedented in the institution's history.

priorTitle: Superintendent of Public Instruction of Virginia (and ex officio member of the University of Virginia board)
notes: A former president of Virginia Agricultural and Mechanical College, he changed the institution's name from Arkansas Industrial University to University of Arkansas in 1899 and created independent departments of history, civil engineering and electrical engineering. He retired in 1902 for health reasons and returned to Virginia.

priorTitle: President
notes: A Baptist minister and educator, he was the first University of Arkansas president born after the Civil War and the youngest person to hold the office. He secured funding for several campus buildings still in use, and later entered educational publishing in St. Louis.

priorTitle: President of the alumni association and member of the Board of Trustees (previously prosecuting attorney and circuit judge, 4th Judicial District of Arkansas)
priorInstitution: University of Arkansas (same institution, internal appointment)
notes: A lawyer admitted to the Arkansas bar in 1883, he came to the presidency from the university's own alumni association leadership and board of trustees. He resigned at the end of the 1911-1912 school year and was elected to Congress two years later, serving seven terms.

priorTitle: Chair of History and Political Science
priorInstitution: University of Arkansas (same institution, internal appointment)
notes: Acting president who reorganized the teaching departments into three colleges (Agriculture, Arts and Sciences, and Engineering) and created a publicity committee that became the university relations office. Despite campus support, the Board of Trustees passed him over for the permanent post.

priorTitle: Chair of the Mathematics Department (and acting president)
priorInstitution: University of Arkansas (same institution, internal appointment)
notes: Longest-serving president in the institution's history; enrollment nearly quadrupled and major campus buildings were constructed during his 26 years. He died in office in a traffic accident near West Fork, Arkansas, on September 12, 1939, while returning from business in Little Rock.

priorTitle: Instructor in law
priorInstitution: University of Arkansas School of Law (same institution, internal appointment)
notes: Elevated from the law faculty (which he joined in 1936) to the presidency at age 34. His presidency was terminated by trustees newly appointed by Governor Homer Adkins, whom Fulbright's mother Roberta, editor of the Northwest Arkansas Times, had opposed; he went on to the U.S. House in 1942, the Senate in 1944, and a long chairmanship of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee.

priorTitle: Registrar and Director of General Extension
priorInstitution: University of Arkansas (same institution, internal appointment)

He mobilized the campus for World War II, saying the University of Arkansas enlisted for the duration when Pearl Harbor was bombed; he resigned in 1946, served into early 1947, and died in Fayetteville that December.

priorTitle: President
notes: An economist recruited from Bennington College who oversaw the racial integration of the university, when Silas H. Hunt enrolled in the School of Law, along with creation of the Fine Arts Center and the Medical Center at Little Rock. He left in 1951 for the Rutgers presidency and later led the National Conference of Christians and Jews.

priorTitle: President
notes: Held a Princeton doctorate and served in the Navy in World War II; at Arkansas he won North Central Association accreditation of doctoral programs, launched the university's first major research push and established a School of Nursing at Fayetteville and the Little Rock Medical Center. He resigned in 1959 for the North Carolina State chancellorship.

priorTitle: Director of University Information
priorInstitution: University of Arkansas (same institution, internal appointment)
notes: Acting president named when John Tyler Caldwell resigned, having joined the university in 1954 as an assistant to the president for public relations. When Mullins was appointed president in 1960 he became vice president for health sciences, later leaving in 1970 for the National Institutes of Health.

priorTitle: Vice President
notes: Came to the presidency after eleven years (1949-1960) as vice president of Auburn University. He retired in 1974; the university's main research library is named in his honor, and he received honorary degrees from Hendrix College (1965) and the University of Arkansas (1987).

priorTitle: Chancellor
notes: An agricultural economist with two decades at North Carolina State before four years as chancellor of the University of Maryland. He built the administrative architecture of what became the University of Arkansas System, creating an executive cabinet and appointing chancellors at the regional campuses, and oversaw construction of Kimpel Hall and a new business building.

priorTitle: Vice President for the Division of Agriculture
priorInstitution: University of Arkansas (same institution, internal appointment)
notes: Promoted from within after joining the University of Arkansas in 1975 as vice president for agriculture. As president he created the chancellor's position at the Fayetteville campus, founded the University of Arkansas Press, and built the Center for Continuing Education; he left in 1984 to become president of his alma mater Auburn University, retiring there in 1992.

priorTitle: President
priorInstitution: Arkansas State University, Jonesboro (a different Arkansas public system, not the UA System)

notes: 4th president; took office February 1994 after serving as provost/executive VP at Rowan. First African American president of a major metropolitan university in Ohio. Died in office March 29, 1998.

priorTitle: Dean of the School of Medicine
notes: 5th president; an internal promotion, having led the Boonshoft School of Medicine as dean (1990-1998). Served until David Hopkins took office in early 2007.

priorTitle: Provost
notes: 6th president; an internal promotion, having served as WSU provost from 2003. Appointed July 2006, took office February 1, 2007. Retired early (effective March 17, 2017) amid a budget crisis.

priorTitle: Retired university president (formerly led National-Louis University, CSU Long Beach, Millikin University, University of North Florida)
notes: Veteran of four university presidencies, brought in as interim president March 17 to June 30, 2017 during WSU's budget crisis.

priorTitle: Chancellor
priorInstitution: Missouri University of Science and Technology (Missouri S&T)
notes: 7th president and first woman to lead WSU; came from the chancellorship of Missouri S&T. Served July 1, 2017 to December 31, 2019, stepping down midway through her appointment.

priorTitle: Provost and Executive Vice President for Academic Affairs
notes: 8th president; an internal promotion. Joined WSU as provost in 2018 (from vice provost for faculty affairs at Appalachian State University), was named president October 2019, and took office January 1, 2020. No active presidential search.

priorTitle: Rabbi of The Jewish Center (Manhattan) and Erna and Jakob Michael Professor of Jewish Philosophy
priorInstitution: The Jewish Center / Yeshiva University (internal faculty)
notes: 3rd president and first native-born American to lead YU; credited with saving the institution financially. Served as chancellor 2003-2013; died in 2020. Anchor incumbent in office in 1996.

priorTitle: President and International Director
priorInstitution: Hillel: The Foundation for Jewish Campus Life
notes: 4th president and the first non-rabbi to lead YU; former Hillel international director and Cardozo Law associate dean. Inaugurated September 2003; stepped down in 2017.

priorTitle: Head of Hechal Shlomo (Center of Jewish Heritage), Jerusalem
priorInstitution: Hechal Shlomo, Jerusalem (formerly senior rabbi, The Jewish Center, Manhattan)
notes: 5th president; Modern Orthodox rabbi and scholar who had led Hechal Shlomo in Jerusalem and earlier served as senior rabbi of The Jewish Center. Began tenure June 5, 2017; still serving.
